title: SRE ops standup summary - March 12 2026
content:
Summary for week of 2026-03-08 -> 2026-03-12

Attendees: Leah, Ravi, Morgan, Aisha, Diego (standup rotation: Leah -> Ravi on-call handoff 03/12 0800 PT)

1) Incidents and noise
- Incident: prefix-cache spike (2026-03-11 02:15 -> 03:05 UTC)
  - Symptom: sudden increase in 95th/99th latency for hosted generation endpoints (x-large models). Alert: gen-latency-95 above 750ms for 10m.
  - Pager events: 3 P1 pages (on-call), ~8 P2 followups. Noise: some noisy retries from a downstream client amplified load.
  - Mitigation timeline:
    * 02:18: reroute policy applied to move low-priority customers to cheaper model variant (manual).
    * 02:28: forced cache warmup for hot prefixes on dedicated pools (scripts run by SRE).
    * 02:40: autoscaler bump to burst pools for dedicated fleet; reduced queued requests.
    * 03:05: latency returned below SLO; incoming traffic normalized after client-side fix rolled out by partner.
  - Root cause (initial): client started replaying sessions after a partial network flake; large number of near-identical prompts bypassed prefix cache (cache key mismatch due to newline normalization edge-case).
  - Action items from incident:
    1) (Ravi) Add newline-normalization to prefix cache key generation in serving-runtime (PR created, see linked GH PR). Due: 2026-03-19.
    2) (Morgan) Add runbook step to detect cache key churn and automated small-batch cache seeding for top-k prefixes. Due: 2026-03-18.
    3) (Aisha) Add a short dashboard for cache-key-uniqueness metric and alert if > 3x baseline in 15m. Due: 2026-03-17.

- Incident: partial metrics ingestion delay (2026-03-09 13:00 UTC)
  - Symptom: gaps in service-level metric aggregation for ~20 minutes; affected historical query panels.
  - Cause: sidecar consumer backpressure after a transient spike in events; consumer lag was within set threshold but combined with a transient storage GC made ingestion latency visible on dashboards.
  - Mitigation: increased sidecar consumer parallelism and temporary routing to secondary aggregator.
  - Follow-up: (Diego) propose a durable buffer for critical SRE-metrics events. Ticket: SRE-4901. Due: 2026-04-02.

2) SLOs & error budget check
- Generation availability SLO: 99.9% monthly target.
  - Current burn rate this month: 0.6% (projected spend 1.8% by EOM if current trend holds) — still green but monitoring.
- Embeddings SLO: 99.95%
  - No breaches this week; one transient spike during cache incident but did not violate.
- Latency SLO (p95 < 500ms for small models, p95 < 750ms for large)
  - Large-model p95 hit 820ms during the prefix-cache incident window; this produced an SLO warning but not a monthly breach.
- Notes: recommend temporarily tightening canary thresholds for customers using large variants until cache key normalization deploys. (Owner: Leah)

3) On-call handoffs and playbooks
- Handoff notes (Leah -> Ravi, 2026-03-12 08:00 PT):
  - Ongoing: prefix-cache PR in review, cache-key dashboard in flight, metrics buffer spike ticket assigned.
  - Suspected recurring pattern: unusual client replay behavior on Partner-X. Liaison: Morgan to coordinate with Partner-X eng.
  - Escalation path: for multi-region latency spikes, default to region-fallback routing and then SRE paging.
- Playbook adjustments this week:
  - Add "verify cache key normalization" as a step in the generation latency playbook. (Morgan)
  - Clarify when to enable burst pools vs autoscaler tuning (new checklist inside runbook). (Leah)

4) Runbook and docs changes
- Proposed edits pushed to confluence runbook draft: add a short section on "prefix cache key hygiene" including examples of keys that bypass cache. (PR to runbook updated by Morgan).
- New quick-reference: one-page checklist for first 10 minutes of a latency P1 (aim: reduce cognitive load for on-call). (Owner: Aisha).

5) Capacity and maintenance notes
- GPU capacity: dedicated pool utilization averaged 68% this week; predicted growth from a new customer trial will add ~5% sustained load in two weeks. Proposal: enable a soft-autoscale threshold at 72% to trigger extra burst nodes earlier. (Diego to propose sizing).
- Planned maintenance: infra team to roll a kernel patch on dedicated hosts (2026-03-19 02:00-04:00 UTC). Expected impact: short rebalances, no customer-facing downtime due to capacity redundancy.

6) Monitoring & alerts tuning
- Reduced noisy alerts: suppressed duplicate trace alerts from legacy tracing agent (temporary suppression applied).
- Next alert tuning: lower sensitivity of "inference-queue-length" for low-priority tenants to reduce false pages. (Action: Leah + Platform Eng).

7) Open questions / decisions needed
- Do we want to push newline-normalization as hotfix to production branches or wait until full CI on main? (Leah: recommend hotfix to prod given incident impact; RFC acceptance needed from Release Eng).
- Should we enforce a client-side recommended retry backoff in SDKs for public customers? (Product input required)

8) Action items recap (all dates in ISO)
- Ravi: implement cache-key normalization change in serving-runtime (PR: linked). due: 2026-03-19
- Morgan: runbook edits + cache seeding script. due: 2026-03-18
- Aisha: cache-key uniqueness alert/dashboard. due: 2026-03-17
- Diego: durable metrics buffer proposal + capacity sizing for autoscale. due: 2026-03-30
- Leah: coordinate with Release Eng on hotfix path + adjust canary thresholds. due: 2026-03-14

Notes to self:
- Add a short retrospective blurb to next weekly update with TL;DR timeline and customer impact.
- Keep on-call rotation schedule updated in team calendar (Ravi up next week).

Appendix: quick metrics snapshot (period: last 7d)
- global gen requests/day: 9.4M
- avg p95 latency (large): 360ms (with 820ms peak during incident)
- host CPU utilization: median 42%
- cache hit ratio (generation prefix): 88% baseline -> dropped to 61% during incident

End of notes.
